title: Manibela to hold transport strike on Nov. 23-24
summary: Transport group Manibela on Sunday said it will hold a two-day transport strike from November 23 to 24 amid reports of possible change in leadership in the Land Transportation Office.

blocks.text: Transport group Samahang Manibela, Mananakay at Nagkaisang Terminal ng Transportasyon (Manibela) on Sunday said it will hold a two-day transport strike from November 23 to 24 amid reports of possible change in leadership in the Land Transportation Office (LTO).
Manibela national president Mar Valbuena said that it would be better for incumbent LTO chief Markus Lacanilao to remain at his post to continue what he started.

"Although sabi nga ni (Transportation) Secretary Vince (Dizon) last Friday na wala pa namang kumpirmasyon. Pero kasi gusto natin malaman na sino ba ang nagrekomenda dito? Kanino ba galing?" he told Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday.
(Although as [Transportation] Secretary Vince [Dizon] said last Friday, there is no confirmation yet. But we want to know, who recommended this? Who did it come from?)
"Marami pang kailangan ayusin sa LTO. Nakikita natin na 'yung dapat ilalagay dito, bakit 'di na lang siya dalhin doon sa puwede?" Valbuena added.
(There is still a lot that needs to be fixed at the LTO. We see that whoever is supposed to be placed here, why not just assign him somewhere else where he will fit?)
Manibela said their march would start at 7 a.m. on Monday, November 23 from Agham Road corner East Avenue going to LTO Central Office.

Meanwhile, transport group Alliance of Transport Operators and Drivers Association of the Philippines (ALTODAP) said Sunday that it would not join the strike, noting that it would only be an inconvenience to many commuters.

"Hindi kami sasama diyan dahil unang-una may sarili silang interes. Kaya kung titignan natin, 'yung kanila bang pag-i-strike ay makatuwiran? Ayun lang po ang sinasabi namin," said ALTODAP national president Boy Vargas in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.
(We will not join that because, first of all, they have their own self-interests. So if we look at it, is their strike reasonable? That's all we're saying.)
"Ang tanong ko, sino ang papahirapan mo? Unang-una, papahirapan mo ang mga mananakay...Kung sa gobyerno siya, dapat makipag-usap nang maayos...Gasgas na gasgas na 'yung strike," he added.

(My question is, who will suffer? First and foremost, you are making the commuters suffer... If it's directed at the government, you should hold a proper dialogue... Holding a strike has become way too overused.)
There is no confirmation yet on whether Lacanilao will step down as LTO chief. —KG, GMA News
